decisions.statement: A run under the overlay reads the checkout with the change's bodies over the checkout.
A body the change has is read at the path the change files that body at.
A path the change takes away is not there inside.
A path the change has no body for is read off the checkout.
A body carried over a file keeps the mode that file has in the checkout.
A body carried where the checkout has no file takes the mode a write gives.
A link the change has is made at the path that link is filed at.
A link points where the change says rather than where anything here works out.
A link is read against the folder that link sits in as any symlink is.
Nothing here says which links a change needs.
A run under the overlay begins in the mounted tree rather than in the checkout.
Name resolution reads the mounted tree.
The mount is made inside a user namespace.
The mount goes when the run that made the mount ends.
A run under the mount has a home of its own, which the sweep takes away.
A link a page states under `~` is placed in that home rather than in the real home.
A run under the mount is told where the age key deciphering a secret sits.
A path reaching outside the checkout refuses the mount.
The folders a mount writes to sit under `/var/tmp` rather than `/tmp`.
The folder overlay work goes in is made unreadable by the kernel that made the folder.
A sweep takes that folder away from inside a user namespace of its own.
Nothing here writes to the checkout.
Nothing here spawns a runner.
The run inside is root in that namespace.
Which of the paths a run names the mounted tree has nowhere is answered here.
A path answered that way says whether a removal was carried for it or no body was carried at all.
The reading of those paths says renaming the file mends nothing.
That reading names the call answering what the edits kept would leave.

definition: a change's bodies mounted over the checkout, so a run reads the tree it would make
